The test image shows a cauliflower leaf with large, dark, circular lesions exhibiting concentric rings, surrounded by yellow halos. Some lesions appear to have torn through the leaf. The affected plant part is primarily the leaf, though some discoloration is visible on the upper part of the stem/curd as well.

I will first read the `part_index.md` file to see which diseases affect the leaf. Then I will review reference images, focusing on visual similarity to the test image, and use all 8 image views before making a prediction.

The `part_index.md` indicates that 'leaf' is affected by Alternaria_Leaf_Spot, Black_Rot, and Downy_Mildew. The test image clearly shows severe leaf damage, but also some possible involvement of the whole plant/curd. I will prioritize images related to "leaf" for the initial exploration.

Based on the symptom descriptions, the test image's lesions with concentric rings and yellow halos strongly suggest **Alternaria_Leaf_Spot**. Black Rot describes V-shaped lesions and blackened veins, which is not what I see. Downy Mildew mentions angular light green/yellow lesions and downy growth on the underside, also not matching. Bacterial Soft Rot mentions mushy, discolored interior tissues with a disagreeable odor, which cannot be visually confirmed and does not match the lesions.

I will start by viewing reference images for Alternaria_Leaf_Spot, Black_Rot, Downy_Mildew and Bacterial_Soft_Rot, using one image for each, then re-evaluate.

Based on this initial comparison, **Alternaria_Leaf_Spot** is the strongest candidate due to the visual similarity of the concentric ring lesions and yellow halos.

I still have 4 reference image views left. I will now view two more images for Alternaria_Leaf_Spot to confirm, and then one each for Black_Rot and Downy_Mildew.
